slides.heading: Two Edge Connected Graph
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Two Edge Connected Graph, a very hard graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Undirected adjacency list; is the graph connected and free of bridges (stays connected after removing any single edge)?
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Undirected adjacency list; is the graph connected and free of bridges (stays connected after removing any single edge)? Empty graph counts as true. Tarjan low-link.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A graph has no bridges if every DFS subtree has a back edge reaching above its root.
slides.narration: A graph has no bridges if every DFS subtree has a back edge reaching above its root.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Remove each edge, test connectivity → O(E·(V+E))
slides.narration: Removing each edge and re-checking connectivity is E times V plus E. Tarjan's single DFS finds bridges in linear time.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Compute the lowest reachable arrival time
3. A child with low time above the parent is a bridge
slides.narration: Step by step. First, dFS with arrival times. Second, compute the lowest reachable arrival time. Third, a child with low time above the parent is a bridge. Fourth, check connectivity too.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Definition
slides.narration: A graph is two-edge-connected if it's connected and removing any single edge keeps it connected, meaning no bridges.

slides.heading: Worked example

lines: low[v] = earliest disc reachable via one back edge

slides.caption: Discovery and low times
slides.narration: During DFS, track discovery time and low link: the earliest discovery time reachable from v's subtree with one back edge.

slides.heading: Worked example

lines: edge (v, w) is a bridge if low[w] > disc[v]
any bridge or unvisited vertex → false

slides.caption: Bridge test
slides.narration: If a child's low is greater than the parent's discovery time, the edge between them is a bridge. Also fail if DFS didn't reach everything.

slides.heading: Java solution (1/2)
slides.narration: Has bridge assigns disc and low, recurses into unvisited neighbours, returns true if low of the child exceeds disc of v, and updates low from children and back edges. Then we check all vertices were visited.

slides.heading: Java solution (2/2)
slides.narration: Has bridge assigns disc and low, recurses into unvisited neighbours, returns true if low of the child exceeds disc of v, and updates low from children and back edges. Then we check all vertices were visited.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of v plus e. Space is O of v.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Skip the edge back to the parent, and check every vertex was visited.
